newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Headlines-April 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Headlines-April 7.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- MING PAO -- A new kind of fake U.S. dollar notes called "super notes" which can fool all the note-inspecting equipment in Hong Kong has been found in the territory.

-- SING TAO -- The Alliance in Support of Patriotic Democratic Movements in China will stop giving financial support to overseas pro-democracy groups, but a spokesman said the decision was not due to political pressure from China.

-- TA KUNG PAO --Chinese Finance Minister Liu Zhongli said China will push ahead with financial reforms. He said because related legislation and supervision still needed to be improved, China needed to proceed carefully.
-- The head of the National People's Congress, Qiao Shi, said China was studying the experience of legislatures in Western countries to develop its own legislative system.
-- ECONOMIC TIMES -- U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin said China was facing a tough time winning renewal this year of its Most Favoured Nation trading status.
-- ECONOMIC JOURNAL -- China World Trade Centre was said to be planning to get an H-share listing before July.

-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- Hong Kong has volunteered to spearhead a drive to strengthen clearing and settlement systems across the Asia-Pacific region -- an initiative arising from the Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation finance ministers' meeting.

-- The New York Mercantile Exchange said it was ready to launch its long-awaited overnight Access system in Hong Kong, offering commodities traders the ability to buy and sell all Nymex contracts while the New York exchange was closed.

-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- Secretary of Justice-designate Elsie Leung called on China's government to streamline procedures for one-way permits to Hong Kong so mainland children would not be so desperate to sneak into the territory illegally.

-- After taking over financially troubled Chinese Television Network, Taiwan's Koo Group was holding discussions with Hong Kong cable and television operators for possible cooperation to air CTN programs in the territory.
